chunks: Al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā when they coincide on the day of al-Jumuʿah. He said:

"They came together in the time of ʿAlī عليه السلام, so he said: 'Whoever wishes to come to the Jumuʿah, let him come; and whoever remains seated, it will not harm him, and let him perform the ẓuhr prayer.'"
And he عليه السلام delivered two sermons, in which he combined the sermon of the ʿEid and the sermon of the Jumuʿah.

key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the midday prayer performed if one does not attend Jumuʿah
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: ʿEid al-Aḍḥā, the festival of sacrifice
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: ʿEid al-Fiṭr, the festival marking the end of sawm
key_terms.خُطْبَةَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the sermon of the Friday prayer
key_terms.خُطْبَةَ الْعِيدِ: the sermon of the ʿEid prayer
key_terms.خُطْبَتَيْنِ: two sermons delivered by the Imam
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, the day of congregational Jumuʿah prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when ʿEid and Jumuʿah fall on the same day in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling when ʿEid al-Fiṭr or ʿEid al-Aḍḥā coincides with Friday. It reports that in the time of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, attendance at Jumuʿah was left optional for those who had attended, while those who did not attend were to perform ẓuhr, and the Imam combined the ʿEid and Jumuʿah sermons.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1473 - Al-Halabi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about the Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha if they fall on a Jumu’ah.

Imam (as) said: "This happened during the time of Imam Ali (as), and He said: 'Whoever wishes to attend the Jumu’ah prayer may do so, and whoever stays back, it will not harm him, but he should pray the midday (Dhuhr) prayer.'
Imam Ali (as) delivered two sermons, combining the Eid sermon and the Jumu’ah sermon”.
